description: §15.11.1 worked example (modal toggle), executed: the parent opens the modal by writing `@showModal`; the body's `visible = false` writes back through the bind channel, so the parent's `@showModal` reflects it; the body's `${visible}` read follows the caller's cell. A second instance bound to a different cell (`@other`) is independent: neither instance's writes reach the other's cell. (The example's `${...}` children spread is omitted: it fails every component today, G-COMPONENT-CHILDREN-SPREAD-SYNTAX-REJECTED-E-COMPONENT-021.)
rationale: §15.11.1: 'The compiler SHALL generate bidirectional synchronisation for `bind:` component props. Changes to `@var` in the parent SHALL propagate into the component. Changes to the bindable prop inside the component SHALL propagate back to `@var` in the parent.' Worked example: 'When the user clicks "Close" inside the modal, `visible = false` writes back through the bind channel to `@showModal`, which the parent owns.'
